recentItems.title: First female reservist passes gruelling P Company course
recentItems.description:
The first female reservist to pass the Army's gruelling P Company course has paid tribute to her best friend, an officer in the Household Cavalry who died last year.

Lance Corporal Grace Cussons, who passed the Reservist All Arms Pre-Parachute Selection on the anniversary of Captain Lizzie Godwin's death, said she was the person who inspired her to succeed.

recentItems.title: Royal Navy team aim for record on epic World's Toughest Row
recentItems.description:
A group of submariners are aiming to break the record for a Royal Navy team on the World's Toughest Row.

It will be the first time the senior service team – HMS Oardacious – has been made up completely of ratings, and they are hoping to become the fastest naval crew to complete the race.

More than 40 boats will compete in the challenge from La Gomera in the Canary Islands to Antigua in the Caribbean this winter.

recentItems.title: British Army's counter-drone system takes off
recentItems.description:
With the uptick in drones in both defence and civilian hands, you may have been convinced every military base already had overwatch technology to spot them. In fact, this is only just taking off.

Project Halo Shield has seen one of the first passive counter-drone detection systems deployed at a British Army base in Warminster by the Experimentation and Trials Group.

recentItems.title: Could UK troops end up fighting in Russian stronghold?
recentItems.description:
As the High North gains in strategic importance, the Svalbard archipelago shifts into focus, and while it's Norwegian territory, Russia maintains rights to a presence here under a 1920 treaty.

The UK has committed to strengthening the defence of the High North with increased troop deployments, carrier strike group operations and active leadership in Nato and joint regional exercises.

But does this leave British forces more exposed in a known Russian stronghold?
